text:
alejandra: FYI: CI is green for linux/mac but Docusaurus build fails on Windows agent with 404s for fragment links. Only happens for headings that include code snippets or inline `:emoji:` shortcodes.

kai: example? can you paste one failing anchor?

alejandra: Sure. Heading in docs/sdk/auth.md -> `### Token rotation (example: rotate_token())`
The generated HTML id is `token-rotation-example-rotate_token` on linux, but on windows the anchor becomes `token-rotation-example-rotate\u005ftoken` (underscore escaped differently) and linkcheck claims fragment missing.

docs-bot: docusaurus-build job #7890 failed: 12 broken anchors (windows). Logs: https://ci.redwood/7890/build.log

sophie: I think this is the classic Markdown-to-HTML slugify inconsistency + our custom snippet replacement step. We run a postprocess script that replaces backticks with underscores — maybe it double-escapes on windows.

liam: We saw something similar in the MkDocs emoji fixes thread but that was about stripping emoji. This is about inline code -> underscores. Could be the Node slugify lib version mismatch in the Windows runner.

kai: Quick test: run the Node slugify used by docusaurus on Windows WSL vs native. I suspect a different ICU/locale behavior.

alejandra: I hacked the build to normalize header ids by adding a tiny transform in our docs pipeline: replace non-alphanumeric runs with a single hyphen and trim. Works but feels risky since it changes public anchors.

sophie: Better: keep original anchors but update the linkcheck to canonicalize using the same Node slugify call we use at build time. Then we don't need to patch all docs.

liam: Agree. Two part plan: 1) update linkcheck runner to call the docusaurus slugify utility (same version) when computing fragments; 2) add a CI assertion that the slugify lib version is pinned in package.json.

kai: I'll open a tiny PR to the linkcheck runner. Also add unit tests for headings with inline code, emoji, and parentheses.

docs-bot: PR 4901 opened by kai 12: "linkcheck: use docusaurus slugify for fragment checks"

alejandra: Nice. Also, let's add a CONTRIBUTORS note advising authors to avoid using bare inline code in top-level headings unless they add an explicit id: `### My API {#my-api}`. Keeps stable links.

sophie: I'll add that note and a small lint rule that warns on headings containing backticks in the docs linter.

kai: CI after PR shows windows matrix passes: https://ci.redwood/7905. linkcheck now canonicalizes anchors same as docusaurus.

liam: follow-up task: audit existing anchors and add redirects for any changed anchors (in case external links depend on them). Maybe a static map in netlify/redirects.

alejandra: opened issue #1023 to track redirects audit.

sophie: thanks all. let's merge the PRs and ship the fixes.

kai: merging in 5. :shipit:
